Other streams measure orthogonal quantities with weak environmental coupling, explaining universal weak cross-stream correlations except this pair.

Logging pipeline contains a deterministic algorithmic step (permutation cipher, pseudo-random seed, round-robin queue assignment, or time-bucketing resampler) that interleaves event IDs across streams at acquisition time, making true temporal order hard to reconstruct without reverse-engineering the cipher. This is a design choice, not a bug, and is functionally equivalent to hypothesis 1 (temporal scrambling) from a data perspective.

Pendulum_lab and resonator_lab measure the same or very tightly coupled physical quantity (or both respond to a shared environmental forcing), but are acquired at wall-clock times offset by 0–1 day and independently trial-numbered. The Day 33 variance spike reflects a genuine, sharp environmental event (e.g., seismic activity, thermal shock, or external vibration) that strikes both instruments simultaneously and is therefore visible in both trial streams on the same calendar day. Temporal scrambling (post-hoc interleaving or logged event-ID permutation) explains the universal zero autocorrelation; the anomalous pendulum_lab ↔ resonator_obs correlation (r=0.946 at 3-day offset) reflects the fact that pendulum_lab and resonator_obs measure the same underlying signal but are acquired with a ~3-day wall-clock phase lag and independent trial numbering, creating spurious correlation when trial counts are misaligned relative to true time.

The 100% consistency of event-ID interleaving across all 27 days reflects a fixed design or systematic pattern in this algorithm, not post-hoc scrambling. The universal zero autocorrelation is evidence of rapid environmental fluctuations (impulse noise, high-frequency vibration, or modal switching) that decorrelate readings at lag >0, or measurement noise dominating signal. The Day 33 variance spike in pendulum_lab and resonator_lab is a genuine shared environmental event. The anomalous pendulum_lab ↔ resonator_obs correlation (r=0.946 at 3-day offset) remains unexplained under this hypothesis and demands separate investigation.
